verdict.rationale: Greptile's docs say it reviews every PR "with complete understanding of your codebase." It also indexes existing rule files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, cursor.rules) and keeps a synthesized per-repo knowledge base, which supports convention-aware review. However, the docs never show review comments that trace call sites or related modules beyond the diff, and the community reports about codebase answers come from an older chat Q&A context, not reviews. missing for 10: documented mechanics of cross-file call-site and related-module analysis in reviews, examples of repo-wide context surfacing in review comments, independent hands-on corroboration of whole-repo-aware PR reviews.

support.subject: As a developer, review comments reflect the whole repository — call sites, related modules, existing conventions — not just the changed hunks

citations.quote: Greptile is an AI code review agent that automatically reviews every pull request with complete understanding of your codebase.
Automatically index existing rule files like Claude.md, AGENTS.md, and cursor.rules for richer review context.
Read the knowledge base - Get Greptile's synthesized documentation for an enrolled repository
Create custom rules, upload style guides, and configure repository-specific standards via greptile.json.
